title: Peter’s Peanuts
content:
In the school holidays Peter stayed with his Uncle Joe. Peter helped Uncle Joe in his garden. He helped his uncle dig up some peanuts. "Yum!" said Peter. "I like peanuts!"

Peter took the peanuts. He gave them to his Aunty Kila. "Let’s cook them together," she said.

Peter’s aunty put the peanuts on her fire. She roasted them.

When the peanuts were cooked Aunty Kila took them from the fire. Peter helped her take off the shells. "Ouch!" said Peter. "They’re hot!"

"I am going to make something yummy," said his aunty. She put the peanuts into a big pot.

Aunty Kila put some oil and salt into the pot. Next she put in some ginger and herbs.

Peter helped stir the pot. He took a peanut from the pot. He put it in his mouth. "Yum!" he said.

"Aunty Kila, can I please take some peanuts home? I will grow them in my garden." "Of course you can," said his aunty. Peter went home with his bilum full of peanuts.

At home, Peter planted the peanuts. He gave them water. He watched the leaves grow. Then he watched the flowers grow. He watched the peanuts grow.

At last it was time to dig them up. Peter cooked the peanuts in the fire. He added oil, salt, ginger and herbs. He put the peanuts into bags.

On Saturday, Peter sold them at his mother’s stall.

Comprehension Questions 1. How did Peter help his Uncle Joe? 2. What did Peter do to help his Aunty Kila? 3. What did Aunty Kila do with the peanuts? 4. Why did Peter say ‘Ouch!’? 5. What did Aunty Kila add to the pot with the peanuts? Why?6. Why does Peter want to take some peanuts home? 7. What did Peter do with the peanuts when he got home? 8. What did Peter put his peanuts into, when they were cooked? Why? 9. What did he do with the bags of peanuts? 10 . Do you like peanuts? Has your mum ever cooked peanuts for you? Activity If Peter sold 13 bags of peanuts, how much money would he get?

title: Lebo and Gogo’s Tea Party
content:
Lebo is at Gogo’s farm. She is bored with chasing the animals. “Now you chase me, Gogo!” Lebo shouts as she races past. “Slow down, Lebo,” Gogo says, hurrying to catch up.

Gogo trips over a rock while chasing Lebo. “Ouch!” she screams. Gogo has hurt her ankle.

She comes back from the doctor with a special boot and crutches. “Gogo, come back to the city with us so that we can take care of you,” says Lebo’s mom. “I won’t leave my farm. I will manage on my own,” Gogo replies stubbornly.

“Gogo, you must come. We will have so much fun!” Lebo says, excitedly.

During the drive, Lebo bounces on her seat. She thinks of all the wild adventures she and Gogo will have in the city.

When they arrive at the house, Gogo rests on the sofa.

Lebo dashes into the lounge. “Gogo, Gogo, I know what we can do today! We can go to the mall. There are lots of shops with nice toys and ice cream!” I’m afraid I can’t. The mall is too big and I will get so tired.”

“Gogo, Gogo, I know what we can do today! We can go to the park!” “I’m afraid that won’t work. The dogs in the park will run around and could make me fall again.”

A second later, Lebo’s eyes are wide with excitement. “Gogo, Gogo, I know what else we can do today. Let’s go to the beach.” “I’m sorry, Lebo. I’m afraid my crutches will sink into the soft sand.”

Lebo is quiet while Gogo knits. Suddenly she has an idea.

“Gogo, Gogo, I know what we can do today! Let’s have a tea party. Gogo, you can sit here. I will bring everything to you because you are hurt.”

title: Thank You Atoekthlok
content:
Once, there was a water drop called Atoekthlok living in a puddle in Phnom Penh and one day, raindrops fell from the sky to his village. "Who do we have here? We’ve met new friends!" Baby Raindroppie, the smallest raindrop of them, all shared the story of his journey. Atoekthlok who was listening amongst them enjoyed hearing this from Baby Raindroppie and thought to himself that one day he could travel like Baby Raindroppie.

As the weather become hotter, the puddle started to smell. There were many more mosquitoes. "What is this horrible smell?" Atoekthlok asked. It was the worst smell he has ever smelt. He was very unhappy being in his puddle but Atoekthlok needed to have a BIG courage to leave. One day, Atoekthlok overheard Panya speaking in the puddle, which she visits often now and then. "My mummy said lots of people who drank the water from this puddle became very sick so we must not drink from it!" When Atoekthlok heard this, he was very surprised. "I can’t believe I have made these people sick …"

Atoekthlok felt really sad. So, he decided visited Mr.Birdy who was very bright from reading many books. "Excuse me, I have become very dirty water and I made my friends really sick. I don’t want to hurt anyone, I want to make their lives better. What should I do? Mr. Birdy replied, "Don’t worry. I heard if you go and meet Uncle Vase, who lives in Boeng pea, you can become cleaner!" So, Atoekthlok went on his way to find Uncle Vase.

"Let’s go to see Uncle Vase!" Atoekthlok made up his mind. Before Atoekthlok left, he asked his friends Brown Drop and Black Drop to go with him but they refused to go. Brown Drop said to Atoekthlok. "For us to find Uncle Vase, I know it will be a long and a difficult journey. I will stay here." "I’m a bit scared. What do I do if something happens?" said Black Drop. But Atoekthlok really wanted to find Uncle Vase. "I need to find Uncle Vase and become cleaner!" and so, he set off.

"Hi there, I haven’t see you before, who are you?"asked Flower. "I’m Atoekthlok from Phnom Penh. I heard that Uncle Vase lives in Boeng paeae, and I’m on my way to find him. Why do you look so weak? Are you ill?" asked Atoekthlok. The flower replied "Yes, I haven’t been drinking water for 3 days, because it didn’t rain. I am very thirsty. I really want to drink some water." Atoekthlok thought and said, "If you don’t mind, could I give you some water to drink? Here, drink this." As Flower drank the water, her body started to straighten. "I feel much better! Thank you Atoekthlok. I hope you find Uncle Vase. I’ll be praying."

The next day, Atoekthlok met Cow who had a patchy body. "Who are you? I haven’t seen you before"asked asked the cow. "I’m Atoekthlok from Phnom Penh. I heard that Uncle Vase lives in Boeng paeae and I’m on my way to find him. You look different to cows from where I live." "My body is really itchy! I haven’t washed for three days because it didn’t rain! That’s why I look different, because I am dirty." exclaimed the cow hitting his bottom with his tail. Atoekthlok replied,"I will give you some of my water drops. Use this to wash your body" Atoekthlok took some of his water out of his body and gave it to the cow and so the cow washed himself. "I feel much better now that I’ve washed my body. Thank you Atoekthlok! I do hope you find Uncle Vase," said the cow. As Atoekthlok continued to help others, he felt fresher and fresher.

While Atoekthlok was having a rest for a long journey, he fell asleep by a puddle when Cow Pat appeared next to him. "Who are you? I haven’t seen you before" asked Cow Pat. "I’m Atoekthlok from Phnom Penh. I heard that Uncle Vase lives in Boeng paeae, and I’m on my way to find him to make my body clean." Atoekthlok told his journey to Cow Pat and as he did so, the cholera came closer and closer. This started to make Atoekthlok feel sick and dirty. "Oh, no" said Atoekthlok. Sadly, Atoekthlok had to leave Cow Pat and said, "Maybe we will meet each other next time."

After Atoekthlok had left Cow Pat, he decided to take a rest by a tree nearby. Soon after, he saw a lady with a clean yellow vase. "Could I take a rest here?" asked Atoekthlok. "Who are you? I haven’t seen you before." Asked the Lady Yellow Bucket with the clean yellow vase. "I’m Atoekthlok from Phnom Penh. I heard that Uncle Vase lives in Boeng paeae, and I’m on my way to find him to make my body clean." explained Atoekthlok. "You have been traveling a lot. You can take a rest here. I will shut the lid so that the children don’t disturb you," said the Lady Yellow Bucket.

After Atoekthlok slept for a day, he felt lighter and cleaner. The Lady Yellow Bucket asked Atoekthlok, "My next door neighbor, Red Vase, has invited me over. Do you want to come along?" ‘’Yes, please,’ said Atoekthlok. When he visited at Red Vase’s house, he felt his body becoming cleaner. "Come and visit our house too! Our house is even cleaner.’’ said Mr Blue Bucket. So Atoekthlok went to Mr. Blue Bucket’s house and spent a day there. After spending three days at Bucketshire, his body had become cleaner, but still he had not found Uncle Vase. "I can feel my body becoming cleaner! Thank you for letting me stay!" and he went off to find Uncle Vase.

"Where am I? This road is so narrow!" said Atoekthlok to himself, standing by the Sandy Village. Sand showed interest to Atoekthlok. "Who are you? I haven’t seen you before." asked Big Sandy. "I’m Atoekthlok from Phnom Penh. I heard that Uncle Vase lives in Boeng paeae, and I’m on my way to find him," explained Atoekthlok. "Oh! I know how to get there. Please follow me! " said Big Sandy. Atoekthlok followed Big Sandy down different streets and as he did so, again he could feel his body becoming cleaner. "There, if you walk along this river, you will be able to find Uncle Vase."

As Atoekthlok followed the river, it got darker and colder. But he did not stop. He wanted to find Uncle Vase. So Atoekthlok walked and he walked and he walked and as the sun started to rise, Atoekthlok started to feel the warmth. During Atoekthlok’s mission to find Uncle Vase, Miss Sunshine was following him and asked Atoekthlok, "Who are you? I haven’t seen you before." "I’m Atoekthlok from Phnom Penh. I heard that Uncle Vase lives in Boeng paeae, and I’m on my way to find him. But I’m really cold after walking all night," he explained. At that moment Miss Sunshine shone her light to Atoekthlok, making Atoekthlok feel lighter.

After he left Miss Sunshine, he carried on following the river when suddenly he tripped on something and fell from a bridge. "Whoops."When Atoekthlok opened his eyes, he realized that Unvle Vase saved him."I have finally found you! Thank you for saving me. How did you know that I was coming to find you?" asked Atoekthlok. "I know all the water drops who help others, and I have heard a lot about you," said Uncle Vase as he gave Atoekthlok a big hug. Miss Sunshine, who was secretly following Atoekthlok, saw this and decided to make him into a clean water vapor.

Now that he was a water vapor, he wouldn’t make people dirty and sick anymore. From then on, Atoekthlok wanted to continue to help others. What adventure would happen to him?

Let’s think about... 1. What happens to Atoekthlok, now that he is a water vapour? Draw next part of his journey. 2. How did Atoekthlok become clean? Think about ways that you could drink clean water. 3. Talk about the help you have been given from people and the help that you have given to people around you.

title: Is That a Ghost?
content:
It was the middle of the night. Ronnie was alone in his room. What was that sound? Was it coming from the old temple near his house? Was someone ringing the temple bell? His aunts were asleep in their room and his father was snoring.

No priests were in the temple. No lights were on in the crematory. Ronnie heard tinkling sounds. Where were the temple guards? What if it's a ghost? he thought. That would be terrible. Foxes were howling, a dog was barking, an owl was hooting, and someone was calling Ronnie's name. Maybe a ghost was coming - a headless ghost!

Ronnie saw something approaching. Its huge hands were holding a jagged stick. Its nails were sharpened spears. Its eyes were blood red.

Its mouth was filled with spindly spikes that looked like the bottoms of radishes.Ronnie thought he felt something grab his foot! His neck stiffened and his head exploded with pain.

Ronnie gritted his teeth. His hair stood on end. He was covered in goosebumps. He wet his pants.Fireflies flickered in his room. He thought they were ghosts. He began to cry.

Ronnie shouted, "Who is it? A ghost, a ghost, a ghost?"His father came in and scolded him, "Dhut, dhut, dhut."His aunts came and scolded him too. Then his aunts said, "Let's run and go see." His aunts all grabbed a light, and they all ran in a hurry.

A dog barked as they got closer and a voice shouted, "Oh no!"Someone hiccupped, hic-hic-hic.Someone giggled, he-he-he."Who's there? Who's there?!" Babu asked as he lit the lantern.

As the light filled the yard, they saw who was there: Raju, Tinu, and Chhotada!Ronnie's friends laughed at their trick.Ronnie laughed in relief!

title: What Could I Become?
content:
The teacher tells us to write about what we want to be when we grow up.

Hmm... what do I want to be?Hey, look! That person sells ice cream.

I want to sell ice cream! I can walk around the neighborhood and eat ice cream all day.

Riiing! Riiing!It's time to go home.

Oh look, a mail truck.

It could be nice to be a postal worker. I could travel all around town

Mom is here to pick me up.

I take the train when I go to Grandma's house.

Choo! Choo!I am a train driver! My train travels to faraway cities.Woohoo.

I wonder where that plane is going?

Pilots can go anywhere. Across oceans and continents! I love flying in the sky.

Hooray! I got a package from my dad.

Maybe I could be a marine biologist like my dad.

Then I could dive in the deep sea and play with all of the underwater animals.

I wonder what's inside the box...? Wow! A rocket!

Uh-oh. I fell asleep.

Finally, I know what I want to be. I want to be an astronaut! I want to explore outer space and visit the planets and the stars.

title: What Dany Wants
content:
Dany wants a bike. Dany wants to ride a bike.

Dany wants a motorbike. Dany wants to ride a motorbike.

Dany wants a car. Dany wants to drive a car.

Dany wants a bus. Dany wants to drive a bus.

Dany wants a digger. Dany wants to drive a digger.

Dany wants a Jet Ski. Dany wants to drive a Jet Ski.

Dany wants a speedboat. Dany wants to drive a speedboat.

Dany wants a ferry. Dany is learning how to drive a ferry.

Questions:1. What did Dany want? 2. What did Dany want to drive? 3. Do you think Dany can drive a ferry? Why? 4. What do you want to learn to drive? Why?

title: Who Is Our Friend?

attribution.author: Gerhard Van Wyk, Lara de Groot, Jade Mathieson.

content:
Can you guess who our best friend is? He’s not like us at all.

Our best friend is Bird!

I am Rhino. I get covered in fleas.

Bird eats them all up.

I am Crocodile. I can’t brush my teeth.

Bird pecks them all clean.

I am Giraffe. I can’t scratch my head.

Bird can reach just the right spot.

I am Zebra. I can’t see things far away.

Bird has great eyes, so when he’s watching I’m safe.

Bird might be different, but that’s no problem…

title: Finding Tuntun
content:
"Hey, Tuntun, how could you chew and tear my ball? You’ll be punished, you are not allowed to come inside anymore."

Woof woof…

A while later…

"Tuntun… Tuntun… Where have you gone?"

"Bo, have you seen Tuntun around?""No! Let me find Tuntun with you!"

"Hey twins, have you seen Tuntun around?""No, we haven’t. Maybe he is in the park?""Let’s go find him there!"

"Mango, have you seen Tuntun? I have searched everywhere but he is nowhere to be found.""I’ll help you find him," Mango said."Me too!" Chi Chi called after them.

"Tuntun… Tuntun…"

"Where can Tuntun go?""Perhaps someone has taken him away?""Oh no, then I have to tell Mom right now!"All the kids flocked to the Tip’s house.

BOING BOING… HUFF PUFF…

"Ah! Tuntun… Tuntun…"

"Tuntun, I miss you so much. You are not punished anymore."

title: Puppy’s Birthday Party
content:
Xongyee loves her puppy.

"I want to give puppy a birthday party!" Xongyee said to her mother. The puppy overhead. He was so happy!

Xongyee and her mother went to the market. They bought a birthday cake.

Meanwhile, the puppy left the house. She invited her friends to the party. "Hello, my bird-friends! Please come to my birthday party."

"Hello, my rabbit-friends! Please come to my birthday party."

Everyone went to find the cats. "Hello, cat-friends! Please come to puppy's birthday party!"

Everyone went to find the turtles. "Hello turtle-friends! Please come to puppy's birthday party."

Everyone went home to puppy's house.

Xongyee was going to open the door. She thought the party was a surprise!

Instead, Xongyee was surprised! Everyone had come to puppy's birthday party.

Everyone loved the party! "Happy Birthday, puppy!" they sang.

title: The Journalist
content:
Once there was a girl from Mandalay named Amar. She was known for her stubbornness. Amar got her stubbornness from her family. She grew up beside strong women who worked hard. Her grandmother and later her mother owned a tobacco factory. It was very unusual for women to own businesses in that time.

Like the other women in her family, Amar liked to push boundaries.When she was 10 years old, she enjoyed jumping onto the backs of moving horse carts.When the driver waved his whip at her, little Amar laughed.

Amar was born a fighter, and she grew up to fight for democracy.Her weapon was her pen. She translated important books, and wrote news articles, short stories, and books about people’s lives, called biographies. She fought for democracy and workers’ and women’s rights.

Amar and her husband Hla, another journalist, worked hard and fought together for independence. They started a newspaper, Ludu Thadin-sa, which became popular because it was smart and unafraid to speak the truth. People began to call the couple Ludu Daw Amar and Ludu U Hla. In 1962,a military general named Ne Win seized power through a coup and took over the country. Ludu Daw Amar and Ludu U Hla bravely led the opposition.The military regime harassed and imprisoned them again and again, but they never stopped.

When her husband died, Ludu Daw Amar did not stop.She continued to write until she was 90 years old. Throughout her life, the authorities tried to stop her from writing the truth. But Ludu Daw Amar persisted.

Use these prompts to write your own story on a piece of paper. When are you happiest?What do you love doing? Life can be tough sometimes.Describe a tough moment in your life that you overcame.Tell a story of you future. What do you dream of doing?

Draw your portrait.

title: How did the Rat Snake Lose its Poison?
content:
In a rural village in Cambodia, there lived a beautiful young woman and a handsome young man. They loved each other and decided to marry.Soon after the wedding, the rains began. It rained for many days until, finally, the sky cleared.As the couple walked to their parents' homes, they left footprints on the muddy path.Suddenly, a rat snake appeared. It had poison in its tongue. The rat snake knew that if it flicked its tongue on the footprints left on the ground, the person who left the footprints could die. The rat snake flicked its tongue on the footprints of the beautiful bride and, soon after, she died.

The groom, who had lost his love so soon after his wedding, was heartbroken.He cried for days as he prepared a funeral to soothe the spirit of his bride.The villagers gathered for the funeral.

When he saw the villagers all gathered together, the rat snake asked the other animals, "Why are they having a feast?""What do you mean?" said the rabbit. "They are mourning the death of the bride. They are having a funeral."The mouse added, "The bride is dead, but your poison isn't strong enoughto scare the villagers. If it were, the villagers would hide in their homes shaking in fear."Then the rabbit said, "Your poison is weak. Maybe the villagers think you are no big deal. "The rat snake, who dreamed of being the king of the animals, wanted people and animals to fear him.He thought that fear was the same as respect and dignity.

"If I spit out all of the poison in my body, the villagers will fear and respect me."The rat snake took a deep breath and…"Kaaaaaaaaaa!" spat out every ounce of poison inside him."The rat snake is spitting out his poison!" the animals yelled.

When they saw the poison on the ground, the honey bees, centipedes, snakes, and thorn fish gathered around. They took turns drinking up the poison the rat snack had spat out.Now the honeybees, centipedes, snakes, and thorn fish were poisonous.And what happened to the rat snake?He was no longer poisonous. He slithered away and lived quietly in the woods.

My name is Likkhena and I was born in Cambodia. I lived inKorea for 11 years before returning home. I love reading inthe library. I have always hoped that some of the interestingstories from Cambodia will be introduced to Korea. It is mywish that this story will be a great opportunity to conveya story from my homeland to the readers and give hope toimmigrant women.

Scientists are still using their knowledge, wisdom and advanced technology to search for another "Earth" in the universe where humans can live. There are too many planets in the universe to count. But surprisingly, only the Earth is uninhabitable for humans. This fact gives us special impressions and enlightenment. I am even more impressed with those women from other countries who came to Korea to work together to write. We live in one world. We are a "global family" from many countries. A family must trust each other, rely on each other, and care for each other. A family should offer a hug first, smile first, and give kindness first. A family must be together in pain, overcome suffering together, and walk together. I admire all those who wrote great stories in these "Multi-value, Multi-together" children’s books. Because all of them, despite being tired from working, child-rearing, housekeeping, and caring for the elderly, we are still able to finish their work. And it must have been even more difficult for them to write in Korean. But then, it is an astonishing power they have, that writing one time can’t compare to speaking hundred times. The power to express one’s thoughts more clearly.The power to communicate more politely with other people. The power to educate their children more fairly. They have this power.I recommend that this project should be continued in the future, giving pride and hope to many immigrant women and their families. Kyung-sil Roh Writer

title: What is Gravity?
content:
Hailey Hop loved to ask questions.

At breakfast she would ask, "Why do stars fall?"At lunch she might wonder, "Why are the clouds gray?"The questions could go on all day!

One afternoon, when washing her hands, Hailey saw something unusual. Something that made her ask a question!

"Why is that drop of water stuck in the tap?" she wondered. She watched it closely. And then, it fell!"What happened?" she asked. "What made the water drop?"

Hailey ran to her mom to ask about the water drop.

"Mom, the tap held on to that water drop. She could not join her friends! Then, after I watched for a while, the drop finally plopped down into the sink with the others. How did the little drop get away from the tap to join her friends?"

"I love how curious you are!" her mother said with a smile. "It was gravity that helped the drop of water."

"A great scientist named Isaac Newton discovered it when he sat under a tree and an apple fell down on his head. Just like your drop fell down from the tap!"

"Gravity is a force that pulls everything towards the center of the Earth. That is why we walk on the ground instead of float away!""But Mother, what about things in space? Do they have gravity too?"

"They do! Gravity is not as strong in space, so astronauts and other objects float around. But large things, like planets, are held in their orbits around the sun by gravity."

"Every object in the universe is pulled together by the force of gravity."

"Wow, that's amazing, Mom. Now I have one more question," Hailey said."What is that, my dear?""Can I become an astronaut when I grow up?""Of course," said her mom. "You can reach for the stars!"

THE END

title: Little Fox’s Lies
content:
"Little Fox, why are you late today? Your two friends waited for you and just left," Aunty Rabbit asked Little Fox. "I'm not late, Aunty. School starts late today," Little Fox replied. "Why is that?" "Master Elephant, our teacher, has to go somewhere," Little Fox lied to Aunty Rabbit.

"Little Rabbit didn't tell me anything about this," Aunty Rabbit thought. "She has also left the carrot biscuits I made for her. I better send them to the school." "Here, Little Fox, can you give these biscuits to Little Rabbit?" Aunty Rabbit asked. "Yes of course, Aunty Rabbit. Give them to me," Little Fox said.

"I wonder if the carrot biscuits are tasty? I must eat one and see," Little Fox thought. He ate one biscuit. "Mmmm, these are yummy. I must eat another one." Little Fox ate another biscuit. By the time he reached school, Little Fox had eaten all the biscuits.

"We left for school without you because you were late again. I hope you're not angry," Little Rabbit said. "Not at all. I was studying all night again. That's why I was late," Little Fox lied.

No matter how hard I try, I always end up lying, Little Fox thought.

Not a single carrot biscuit is left for Little Rabbit. What will she eat for lunch? Little Fox wondered.

Their lunch break started and they all sat together to eat. "Oh no, I left my lunch at home," Little Rabbit said. "Let's all share and eat," Little Bear suggested. Little Fox remembered that he ate Little Rabbit's lunch. He realized his friend was hungry as a result of his actions. He felt very ashamed and left the table.

"Where did Little Fox go?" Little Bear asked Little Rabbit. "There he is," Little Rabbit pointed to a tree nearby. They went over to Little Fox.

"Little Fox, are you feeling sick?" Little Rabbit asked. "Why are you crying? Did we do something wrong?" Little Bear asked. Little Fox was touched by his friends’ concern and he felt even worse. He started crying harder. "No no, you guys did nothing wrong. I'm the one who did something I shouldn't have," Little Fox sobbed.

"We all make mistakes," Little Rabbit said. "Maybe talking about it will help. What did you do?" "Yes, you can talk to us about what happened," Little Bear said. "I'm afraid you won't like me after I tell you what I did," Little Fox gulped. "Aunty Rabbit gave me a pack of carrot biscuits when I was on my way to school. She asked me to give them to Little Rabbit but I ate them all." "Please tell me you forgive me? I will never do anything like this again," Little Fox asked.

"Why did you wait so long to tell us the truth?" Little Bear asked. He was a bit angry. "I felt bad for lying to you two. You're my friends and I know lying is not the way to show you I care for you. I wanted to tell you the truth this morning, but I was too scared to say anything," Little Fox explained through tears. "Little Fox, I am upset that you ate my lunch. I would've happily shared it with you. But I forgive you," Little Rabbit said.

"I am glad you told us the truth. But remember, when you lie because you are afraid to speak the truth, people lose trust in you," Little Bear said. "You are right. To be true to myself and my friends I need to take responsibility for my actions. I promise to try harder next time." Little Fox said, wiping his eyes. Little Rabbit and Little Bear offered their hands to Little Fox to stand up. Little Fox was really happy that he told the truth and apologized.

title: I Don’t Want to Eat!
content:
Clarita is a little girl with a BIG dream. She wants with all her heart to have real superpowers! Clarita dreams of running as fast as lightning and seeing tiny insects with her sharp eyes. She wants to help others solve difficult problems.

“Clarita, let’s have some food,” calls mom. “I am busy. I do not have time to eat! I want to be a superhero” replies Clarita.

Clarita runs up and down the street and all around the orchard. After a few minutes, she begins to feel extremely tired. She needs to rest her legs.

“Clarita, let’s have some food and drink,” calls mom later that morning. But Clarita is too busy. She answers, “I do not want to eat! I want to be a superhero.”

In the afternoon, Clarita strains her eyes to look clearly at tiny ants. After a few minutes, she feels her head spinning. She needs to rest her eyes.

“Clarita, let’s have some food and drink, so you can have energy,” calls mom. But Clarita is too busy. She yells, “I do not want to eat! I want to be a superhero.”

In the evening, Clarita helps her brother with a jigsaw puzzle. No matter how hard she tries, she just cannot work out how the pieces fit together.

Clarita runs to her room crying and closes the door. Why doesn’t she have any superpowers? She tries so hard!

Mom comes in and holds Clarita tightly. “I see you really want to have superpowers,” says mom “Clarita, let’s have some food and water, so you can have energy. Food makes our bodies strong and our minds sharp.”

Clarita’s opens her eyes wide. “Does it really?” she asks. Mum smiles and nods.

Mom brings her a plate of food with rice, tofu, and green vegetables. Clarita excitedly eats her food.

Then, Mom offers her a plate of colorful fruits.

After finishing her meal, Clarita is ready to try again. Her body and mind feel energized.

Now, Clarita runs fast around the orchard. She can see the little ants when she looks for them. She can help her brother put the jigsaw pieces in place.

From that day on, Clarita enjoys eating her food. She knows that if she wants to have wonderful superpowers, she must start by eating healthy meals.

.

title: The Cave of Fireflies
content:
Lizzy hated winter. It rained every day and all the insects she loved to eat disappeared.

Lizzy hunted all day for something to eat, but found nothing. When evening came, she collapsed with exhaustion.

The next morning, Lizzy met her friend Gecko. "Have you found anything to eat?" she asked him."Yes! Come with me and I will show you something amazing. Trust me, I know what I'm doing!" he said.

"We'll have to cross swamps and crawl through giant trees, but finally we will arrive at a cave full of fireflies. There are millions of them! We can eat as much as we would like and will never be hungry again.""Let's go now!" Lizzy said with excitement.

Gecko suggested that they leave that night so no one else would follow them."But I can't see well in the dark," Lizzy told him."Don't worry, Lizzy. The full moon will light our way."

Though she was still nervous, Lizzy followed Gecko through the deep swamp. Then, she felt something bump her tail under the water."What was that?" Lizzy whimpered.

Two bright eyes suddenly appeared and moved quickly towards Lizzy and Gecko."An alligator!" Gecko shouted. "Swim away, Lizzy!"

The alligator was just about to gobble Lizzy up when Gecko grabbed a big stick and shoved it in the alligator's mouth.

The two friends made it safely to the riverbank, but it took Lizzy a while to stop shaking."See, I told you I know what I am doing," Gecko said.

As they walked into the giant forest, Lizzy saw something strange above her head. "What are those bright glowing eyes?" she said. "Is there something up in the trees that will chase and eat us?""No, no," said Gecko calmly. "These are just fruit bats. They don't eat creatures like us. Come along, I know what I'm doing."

A bit further down the path, Lizzy stepped on a sharp thorn. "Ouch!" she cried. "What was that!"Gecko laughed, "It's only a porcupine out looking for worms. Let's keep going. You know I know what I'm doing!"

Gecko and Lizzy walked and walked. They walked through most of the night! Lizzy was tired and hungry. All she could think about was eating her fill of fireflies once they reached the cave.But suddenly . . .

. . . a huge owl swooped down and grabbed Gecko in its sharp talons! The owl flew away with Gecko before Lizzy could do anything.

"Oh, what will I do now!" Lizzy cried. "Gecko knew what he was doing, but I do not. Now I will never find the cave of fireflies!"

Then, something fell from the sky and landed right on top of Lizzy with a thump."Oof! What was that?" she cried.

The thing from the sky stood up and laughed. "It's me, Lizzy. Gecko!""How did you escape?" Lizzy asked, astonished."I sacrificed my tail to the owl. But don't worry, it will grow back soon. See, I know what I'm doing."

Finally, the sun began to rise. Birds began to sing and fly from their nests. Lizzy and Gecko could see a cave up ahead!

"We did it!" Lizzy shouted. "Thank you my expert friend! Let's eat!""It was nothing," Gecko replied.

But as they stepped inside the cave, a huge dragon lizard opened its mouth and hissed at them!Lizzy and Gecko had never seen anything so frightening. They ran as fast as they could away from the cave."Someone must have shared my secret!" Gecko fumed as he pulled Lizzy to safety. "I would rather keep searching for grasshoppers than face that dragon again!" "Gecko, it's time to go home," Lizzy said. "It's this way. Trust me, I know what I'm doing!"

The End

title: Abdul Kalam: A Lesson for My Teacher
content:
While the author, illustrator, and publisher of this book encourage and support translation of this work into other languages, they request that substantive changes to the text and art be kept to a minimum.

I lived on the Mosque Street in Rameswaram, a city famous for its Shiva temple. Every evening on my way home from the mosque, I would linger near the temple.

I always felt like a stranger there, as the temple goers stared suspiciously at me. They probably wondered what a Muslim boy was doing in front of a temple.

The truth was that I loved to listen to the rhythmic chanting of the mantras, though I never understood a word. There was a strange magic in them.

Of course, something else led me there. My best friend, Ramanadha Sastry, was the son of the head priest. He would sit beside his father at this hour, reciting hymns. Ram would steal a smiling glance at me from time to time.

At school, Ram and I always sat together on the first bench of our classroom. We were like brothers. However, being a Hindu priest’s son, he wore a sacred thread, while my white cap marked me as a Muslim.

One day, when we were in the fifth standard, a new teacher came to our class. He looked strict. He went around the class tapping his cane on his palm and stopped before us.

"You, the one in the white cap," he shouted. "How dare you sit beside the temple priest’s son! Go sit on the last bench." I felt hurt. With tears in my eyes, I picked up my books and shifted to the last row.

Ram and I wept together silently after school. We thought we would not be allowed to be friends anymore.

When I reached home that day my father looked at me and asked: "Were you crying... What’s wrong son?" I recounted the whole incident to my father, while Ram told his family the same story.

Early the next morning, Ram came running to our house and said: "Father has asked you to come to our house immediately." I was terrified. I thought I was in for some more trouble.

We hurried back to Ram’s house. My heart skipped a beat when I saw our new teacher standing there.

"In the light of our discussion, apologise to Kalam here," said Ram’s father with a stern face. I could not believe what I had just heard! The head priest was asking the teacher to apologise to me?

"No child is less than another in God’s eyes," Ram father said. "It is your duty as a teacher to help students live in harmony in spite of the differences in their background. You can no longer teach in this school."

Our teacher immediately asked me to forgive him. He hugged me and said: "I am sorry, Kalam. I have learnt an important lesson in life today."

Ram’s father saw that the teacher sincerely regretted his behaviour and permitted him to continue teaching.

From that day on, Ram and I sat together proudly on the front bench. We have remained the best of friends ever since.

title: The Journey Home
content:
It is time for Greena to lay eggs at the beach where she herself hatched. “Come and swim with us, Greena!” the dolphins invite her cheerfully.

Greena declines because she prefers to swim alone.“Thank you, but I am taking another route.”Greena turns around and changes direction.

Wow, a school of jellyfish!Their dance is so impressive.Greena sways along with them.She swirls and soars. She moves up and down.

Whew! This jellyfish dance is exhausting.

Greena continues her journey.Oh no! She has gone astray from her chosen route.

When Greena turns, suddenly, a group of tuna glides close by. Wow! Greena wishes she could swim as fast as they can.

One, two, three, swoosh!Greena dives through the water.Paddle, kick, paddle, kick.

Whew! Following the group of tuna is tiring.Greena tries her best,but turtles can’t swim as fast as tuna. Soon, the tunas’ tails appear smaller, and they are gone.

Oh, oh! Greena is off her course again.Trying to keep up with the group of tuna has caused her to lose focus.

Greena feels calmer among the coral.Hey, what are those clown fish up to?They flit around among the sea anemones.

They are cleaning the anemones.Greena hears the clownfish call out to each other,“Let’s clean up!”“Our home must be as pretty as the fan-shaped coral, where the pygmy seahorses live."

Greena has to continue her journey,But she is curious about the pygmy seahorses.Greena decides to drop by, just for a while.

Greena examines the coral closely.Two little dots are blinking.They are the eyes of the pygmy seahorse.

Their home is really pretty.Greena loves it there.But it is time for Greena to continue her journey.

Suddenly, a big wave passes through.A manta ray glides gracefully.Greena flaps her flippers like the manta.

But, why is Greena following the manta ray?She is going further away from the island she wants to reach.

Argh! Greena is annoyed at herself.The journey home is going to be longer.

Sighing, Greena swims slowly.She hears the distant call of the dolphins.

“Hi, Greena! We thought you would have reached shore. We have been around twice already.” The dolphins cry out in surprise.

Greena is relieved to see the dolphins. This time she is going to swim together with them.That way, she will stay on course.

The seagulls’ calls catch Greena’s attention.This time Greena just waves at them.She has to go home.

She sees the shoreline.Greena smiles. Finally, she is back at the beach where she hatched.

Get to Know MoreGreena is a green sea turtle (Chelonia mydas). Turtles are reptiles that live is sea water. Their soft body is covered with a carapace, a hard shell for protection. During nesting season, turtles swim back to the shore where they hatched. They dig a nest to lay their eggs, and then crawl back into the ocean. The illustration for this story has been adopted from the Wayang Samudra characters found at the Center for Marine Conservation, Coral Triangle Center (CTC), a conservation education center in Sanur, Bali. The Wayang Samudra is a shadow puppet of sea animals created by Sujono Keron and Sih Agung Prasetya together with the CTC.

title: Unni’s Wish
content:
THUMP, THUMP, THUMP! The noise wakes up Unni and he looks outside the window. Some men are digging and hammering near his home. There are thick wires and wooden poles all around them. Unni wonders if they are building a new house in the forest.

Unni finds Amma pressing his school uniform with a clothes iron full of hot coal. "Amma, who are these men working outside our home?" asks Unni. "You’ll find out soon. Now go and eat your idlis before they become cold," replies Amma, with a mysterious smile.

After breakfast, Unni pulls on his warm uniform. "Bye, Amma!" Unni hurries through the forest towards the coffee estate. His best friend Ammu lives here. There she is, waving at him! "Let’s race!" says Ammu. And off they go!

The two friends zip through the coffee plants. They circle around the big mango tree. They hop across the stream. And finally, they reach the road that leads to school.

Unni hears Ammu humming a tune as they walk to class. It’s from her favourite cartoon show on TV. "The boy in the cartoon fights villains using his magic glasses!" she explains. Unni wonders when he will have a TV at home.

TRINGGGGG! The school bell rings. Unni and Ammu hurry to catch the bench under the fan. What a wonderful breeze! Unni imagines sleeping under a fan at home. It would be great in the summer!

At break time, Unni and his friends run out to play. It’s a very hot day and they soon get thirsty. They go to Kuttan Chettan’s shop to buy lime juice. BRRR! The glass feels cold in Unni’s sticky hands! "If we had a fridge at home, Amma’s lime juice would taste this good," Unni mumbles to himself.

Unni’s head is bursting with questions. He decides to find Janaki Miss. "Kuttan Chettan’s shop has a fridge but we don’t have one at home. There’s a fan at school but we don’t have one in our room. Ammu has a TV at home but I don’t. Why is that, Miss?" asks Unni.

"Where do you stay?" Janaki Miss asks. "In the forest, Miss. Beyond the coffee estate." "Oho! Lights, fans, fridges and TVs need electricity to work. It sounds like your home doesn’t have an electricity connection." "But why?" asks Unni. Janaki Miss replies, "Electricity comes through wires from the village power station. Since you live deep in the forest, it is difficult for the wires to reach your home." Unni is disappointed.

After school, the two friends race back to Ammu’s home in the coffee estate. The sun is setting. Ammu turns on the tubelight. "I’m going to go study now," she says. "It's getting dark. Let me get home quickly. I need to light the kerosene lamp," says Unni, sighing.

Outside their house, Unni sees his father talking to some men. It’s the men who made all the noise in the morning. "What is happening, Acha?" Unni asks.

Everyone turns and smiles at him. Amma points to a switch on the wall. Unni presses the switch and... TA DA! THE ROOM LIGHTS UP! Everyone claps. This can only mean one thing... "I can’t believe it!" says Unni. "Our house finally has electricity!"

Unni can now study under the tubelight, sleep under the fan, drink chilled lime juice, and finally watch the adventures of the superhero with magic glasses!

Did You Know? - Electricity can be created in many ways. In India, it is mainly produced by burning coal. - We also generate electricity from water, wind and sunlight. - In 1905, Bangalore became the first city in India to get electricity. - Some places in India still don’t have electricity. The state of Bihar has the most number of houses without electricity. Uttar Pradesh, Jharkhand and Odisha are some other states where many people continue to live without electricity.

Flash Quiz! 1. Sometimes you can spot a flash of electricity in the sky. What is this called? 2. Unni wants his home to have electricity so that a TV, fridge, tubelight and fan can work. Can you name three other things that work on electricity? 3. This fish produces electricity to hunt and also to protect itself from danger. Do you know what it’s called? 4. In 2017, a south Indian state became the first in the country to provide electricity to every household? Which one is it?

Answers 1. Lightning 2. Iron box, computer, cell phone, geyser, etc. 3. Electric eel 4. Kerala

title: The Shy Moon
content:
The moon rises.

To his right, a group of stars play with each other.

To his left, a group of stars chat with each other.

It looks like they are having a lot of fun, but I am all by myself, thinks the moon.

What if I try talking to them?The moon slowly moves toward the group of stars.

Will they play with me? I am so different from them.I should try.

The moon moves forward again, and then pauses again. He still feels shy.

The moon takes out a paintbrush.He writes, "Hello."Then the moon erases the word. He starts again, and then erases.

The moon draws, and then erases. There are marks all over the his surface.

It looks like they have been playing and not noticing me. I will just go and clean myself up.

Then, the moon hears a voice behind him. "What are those marks on you?" The moon turns around and sees the stars staring at him.

The moon smiles shyly. "Hello, can I play with you?"

The stars laugh. "Aren’t we already playing?" they say.

A star asks, "What were you drawing?""Take a guess," says the moon.I think you drew letters," the star replies.

"No, I think that is a drawing of us," says another star."I think it looks like a rabbit," a third star chimes in."Moon, please just tell us! What were you drawing?"

The moon grins. "I do not know what I drew, either."They all laugh.

"How about we stars gather into different shapes and you guess what we are?" a star suggests.

The moon and the stars play together for the rest of the night.

title: Sour Fruits, Sweet Friends
content:
Four fruit trees are neighbors in the forest. The bilimbi, tamarind, and calamansi fruits get along. But they don’t like the fourth fruit, batuan. How sour of them!

Early one morning the four fruits came down from their branches.“Come on, let’s play!” called Wanda, the batuan.The other three fruits didn’t reply. They ignored Wanda. They were so sour, and so were their manners!

“Come on, let’s sing!” Wanda called again.The three fruits still didn’t reply. They were very sour, and so were their manners!“Come on, let’s dance!” the batuan called a third time.

Olin, the bilimbi, raised her eyebrows.Tamar, the tamarind, rolled his eyes.Edan, the calamansi, pursed his lips.“We don’t want to, Wanda!” they told her all together.

Wanda climbed back up her tree,and sat all alone on a branch. She saw her reflection on a dew-covered leaf. She touched the dents and dark spots on her skin.

Because of her odd appearance, Wanda wasn’t treated fairly. Nobody cared about her. Nobody played with her.While the other three were happily playing without her, she at least enjoyed watching them and looking after them.

“Watch out!” Wanda cried when she saw weaver ants approaching.The three fruits froze in fright.Then they turned around, terrified, and ran back up their trees.

Olin, Tamar, and Edan climbed onto their branches and hid beneath their leaves. Peering out from behind their leaves on alert, they worried that the weaver ants might find them and bite them.

Wanda ran to hide behind her leaves, which she also used as a body shield.She peeked out at the other fruits to see if they were okay.“Please keep Olin, Tamar, and Edan safe,” she earnestly prayed.

“Are you okay, Olin! Tamar! Edan!?” Worried, Wanda couldn’t help but ask.The three fruits didn’t reply. They ignored Wanda.Oh, how sour!

The weather turned sour, too! The sky turned gloomy. The wind blew loudly, and the rain fell hard!Woosh! Woosh! Woosh!Strong wind blowing! Heavy rain pouring!

The weaver ants and leaves were swept away.Wanda, Olin, Tamar, and Edan gripped their branches with all their might.“Hold on tight!” exclaimed the batuan.The three fruits didn’t reply. They were very quiet.

Olin, Tamar, and Edan were too scared to answer.The trees were swaying in the strong wind and heavy downpour.Woosh! Woosh! Woosh!They seemed to break, swaying and shaking.

When the storm ended, Olin, Tamar, and Edan thought about how close they had come to losing each other and losing Wanda. They stopped mistreating Wanda. The four forest neighbors became close friends. United and helping each other, they’re the four fruit trees: bilimbi, tamarind, calamansi and batuan.Such sour fruits, but their camaraderie is sweet.

Wonderful Wordsbatuan - a sour, round fruit that grows on wild trees in southern Philippinesbilimbi - a small oval fruit with crisp skin and very sour juicetamarind - a brown pod-like fruit that contains a sweet tangy pulpcalamansi - a sour lemon-like citrus fruit native to the Philippines

title: Rooftop Garden
content:
The view from Tita’s rooftop is not very beautiful. There is a large factory that spouts smoke behind her home. So Tita decides to put some sunflowers on the roof to make it prettier.

But the sunflowers soon wilt. Tita wishes she could have flowers on the roof all the time. But how will she do it?

On the weekend, Tita asks her father if he will help her. "I want flowers here all the time, Dad. But how will we keep them alive?" she asks."We will plant a garden! I have brought a large container for soil and seeds to plant. We will work together to help this garden grow and thrive for a long time."

Her family works hard to prepare the soil for planting. But when Tita starts to dig in the dirt, she gets a surprise."Worms, yuck!" she exclaims."Worms are important for a garden, Tita," her father says. "They help the plants to grow."Tita is not sure she likes worms yet, but she will keep them if they will help her garden.

When it is time to water the plants, Tita pours a whole bucket of water on the plants. "Drink up seeds, so you will grow quickly!" she tells her plants."Stop, Tita! Not so much," Tita's mother says. "The plants only need a little water at a time."

"But I want them to grow up fast!" Tita complains. "A garden needs time to grow," her mother reminds her gently. "I know it is hard, but you must be patient."

A week later, the seeds have begun to sprout! It is time to transfer each plant into its own pot. Tita is excited. She rushes to tug the plants out of the soil. "Be gentle, Tita," her mother says. "If you break off the roots, they will not grow."

Together, Tita's family plants the little sprouts in new pots. Then Tita’s father begins to make boxes for more flowers to grow. Tita makes a sign for her garden.

Tita has learned everything she needs to know about caring for her garden. Before long, the flowers begin to bloom!

One evening, Tita picks some of her sunflowers to display on the dinner table. As she carries the flowers inside, she notices her mother cooking some vegetables."Mom, can we grow vegetables in our garden too?" "What a great idea, Tita! Let’s do it."

Before long, Tita’s garden has covered the roof. She is growing flowers, carrots, onions, eggplants, and many other wonderful (and delicious) things!

Now everyone in the neighborhood enjoys the view of Tita’s garden instead of the smoky factory. They all ask her for advice on planting. Maybe next year they will make rooftop gardens too!

title: The Golden Scale
content:
Mr. Sengolan has a golden scale in his classroom. He received it as a gift for his various accomplishments, including being one of the best teachers. From time to time he would show the golden scale to his students and tell them about kings who were renowned for their honesty.

Mr. Sengolan's class has their exams today. The students with the highest scores will be awarded scholarships. This is a very important exam for Uttaman who lives with his mother. Surprisingly, Mr. Sengolan wasn’t at school today. Uttaman needed to find him. “Where did Mr. Sengolan go?” he asked, looking everywhere.

Uttaman felt weighed down by his bag, as if the books weighed a ton. He slowly walked towards the exam hall. His sturdy legs, used to walking almost two kilometers every day, were wobbling today. “Did you see Mr. Sengolan?” he asked every friend he saw.

“No, we haven't seen him,” they answered. “But Uttama, you look like you've studied all night without sleeping. Your eyes are red and they are tearing up.” In reality, Uttama had neither slept nor studied. He was troubled. He didn’t know what to do, so he kept looking for the principal.

Uttaman found the principal. He wasn’t in the mood to listen to Uttaman. “Why are you here? The exam will start soon. Go and complete it,” he insisted. Go get the best score." Uttaman was a really bright student, but the principal's words weren't encouraging.

“Oh man, what to do now?” Uttaman didn’t even want to think about what would happen if he failed. He heard his friend calling, “Uttaman, please come here quickly. They're going to start the exam!”

There were specific questions he was hoping wouldn’t be on the exam. “Dear God, please, don't make me answer those questions,” he prayed while sitting in the exam hall. But when he got the paper, all the questions were the ones that he didn’t want to answer. Uttaman finally made a sure decision. “I'm not going to fill out the exam," he said to himself. Suddenly he felt good. His legs stopped wobbling and the bag didn’t feel heavy. All was right.

Finally, the award day came. “Uttaman, the principal asked you to come to the office,” a teacher told him. “I think you have the highest score,” his classmate said. “We all know you're very bright.”

The principal looked upset. Mr. Sengolan looked concerned. “Uttaman, what happened? You didn't answer any of the questions on the exam. Why did you do this?" he asked. Uttaman looked down with tears in his eyes. “You didn't know the answer to any of the questions?” the principal asked again. “I knew the answers to all of them, Sir,” Uttaman said calmly.

“Then why didn’t you write the answers on the paper? Were you sick? Is your arm broken? Show me!" Mr. Sengolan said worriedly. Uttaman handed a book to Mr. Sengolan. “ Sir, you gave me this book to study from. Please open it and look inside,” Uttaman said.

Mr. Sengolan opened the book and was in shock. Inside the book was the answer paper that he'd been looking for everywhere. “I only realized it was the answer paper after reading through it. How could I take this competitive exam after seeing the answer paper?” asked Uttaman. The principal and Mr. Sengolan were speechless.

Later that day, everyone attended the awards ceremony, including Uttaman’s mother. The principal delivered a speech. “Uttaman is a student just like all of you. A child,” said the principal. Mr. Sengolan joined the principal on stage. He brought his golden scale. “I am going to present this to one of my students who was very honest,” he said. “Come on stage, Uttaman.” Mr. Sengolan presented his golden scale to Uttaman as a token of appreciation for his honesty.

title: Mulmul and the Butterfly
content:
Mulmul was a small fluffy rabbit. She lived in the hollow of a tree in a huge forest. She liked to eat carrots. One afternoon she went for a walk.

In a flower garden she saw a caterpillar sitting on a leaf. It was eating the leaves of the flower. Mulmul thought to herself, If I eat more and take a long nap, I'll wake up as a butterfly!

Mulmul took carrots out of the bag and ate them while the caterpillar munched on the leaves.

After eating, they both fell asleep.In the morning, Mulmul opened her eyes and saw that the caterpillar had turned into a beautiful butterfly! "Wow!" Mulmul said. "You look so beautiful! If only I could be a butterfly." Mulmul felt sad as she said goodbye to the butterfly.

As Mulmul kept walking she found lychee trees on the slopes of the hills. Mulmul was tempted to eat the sweet ripe lychee. But the fruits were high up and the hills were steep. Determined, Little Mulmul tried to climb the lychee tree.

Suddenly, her hand slipped and she began to fall. Hearing a scream, the butterfly friend flew to the hills.

As she was falling, Mulmul's foot caught on a branch. Without knowing how she did it, she jumped. And just like that she jumped from one branch to another until she landed on the ground. "Wow," the butterfly said, amazed as he reached the hills. He was happy to see that Mulmul was okay.

Rain began to fall, deflating Mulmul's spirit. "I can't do anything. I can't fly like a butterfly, I can't even climb a tree!" she said angrily. The butterfly saw that Mulmul was frustrated. He didn't know how to make her friend feel better. He flew away so at least Mulmul wouldn't have to watch him fly.

Suddenly, the butterfly got caught in a spider's web! He tried again and again to move his wings, but he couldn't free himself at all. The spider began to slowly wrap the butterfly with its thread! Afraid for his life, the butterfly shouted, "Save! Save me!"

Mulmul raised her long ears as she heard someone saying from a distance, "Save me, save me!" She ran towards the sound and found the butterfly was trapped in a spider's web. Mulmul said, “You're up so high. How can I save you? ” Butterfly said, "You can. You can save me just as you saved yourself on the hill.”

Mulmul finally realized that she had saved her own life. "This time I'll save my friend's life too!" she said to herself. She jumped from one branch to another, higher and higher into the tree, and freed the butterfly from the web.

Both of them came down to the ground safely. Butterfly said, "Mulmul, you saved my life today! Thank you so much!" Mulmul replied, "My friend, I got very hungry from all that jumping! I haven't eaten a single carrot all day!" They both laughed and went in search of carrots. Mulmul jumped the whole way!

title: Shock! Crash!
content:
“Titay, where is the vinegar and soy sauce that I asked you for? Mother asked.“I haven’t seen it, Mama,” Titay replied.“You couldn’t find it or you haven’t opened the box yet? Mother asked.

“If I didn’t watch TV, I wouldn’t be asked to do errands.”Titay slowly crawled outside but her brother saw her.“Titay where are you going? You haven’t made your bed yet,” her brother said.“I’ll do it later kuya,” Titay replied.“My beautiful sister, do it first,” replied her brother.

“One, two, three, four,” she counted as she cleaned.“Fluff the pillows, fold the blanket, pick up the banana peel, put away the scattered books.”

While cleaning, Titay saw Cora from the window playing chase.“They are playing while I’m cleaning. Hmmm, I’m not Cinderella. I’m Titay.”Titay looked out the window. “It’s too high, I can’t jump out.”She checked the door, then sneaked out.

“Oh, are you done? That was fast,” her brother said. “Well, that’s me,” she boasted.“Wow! That’s my girl. Now, you better help your brother cut these beans.” Mother said.“Here we go again,” Titay thought.

“Yes mother, but first I need to pee.” Then, Titay walked to the kitchen and went out through the other door.“Titayyyy!!!! Her mother called.“I wish my name wasn’t Titay,”

“Kuya, can I ask something?”“Sure,” her brother replied.“Kuya, did papa and mama teach you the household chores?”“Yes, papa and mama showed me how to do the chores, then we did them together, then I did them on my own,” explained her brother.

“Ah, that’s why papa and mama showed me how to do the chores, just like they showed you!” Titay answered.Her brother laughed. “Why do you think they did that?" asked her brother. “So, I would know how when I grow up,”Titay answered. “Wow! That’s right sister,” he said.But in her mind, she just wanted to play.

After eating lunch, Titay began doing the dishes in a hurry. “Cora’s group is waiting for me. If I don’t show up, they will replace me. What should I do? Aha! I know.” She smiled to herself. Then, she quickly put the dishes in the cupboard and left.

Kablang! Crash! Titay heard something crash in their kitchen. She ran back inside and saw the broken dishes on the floor. The cat was licking the plates.Her mother also hurried to the kitchen.

“I’m sorry Mama, I did something wrong. I should have washed the dishes before I put them away and left to play.” Titay apologized.“I expect that it won’t happen again.” stressed her mother.

Titay was sad and had no appetite that night. Her favorite plate and glass were broken. Those were gifts from their grandma. Now she wouldn’t be able to use them anymore.

title: Vroom! Vroom!
content:
Biru was waiting for Alma to finish her classes. There she was! Biru and Alma were going to take orders as an online motorcycle taxi. It was their first day. Biru was worried. Could he handle it?

“Let’s get ready,” Alma said. Gasoline? Check! Oil? Check! Tires? Check! Seeing Alma so confident calmed Biru’s nerves. He was ready to go.

Ring! Ring! Wow, an order already. “Let’s go!” Alma cheered.Biru revved his engine in excitement. Vroom, vroom!

The streets were packed. “Hi! Hello! How are you?” Biru politely greeted the other vehicles. Beep, beep!Vroom, vroom! Honk, honk!

Biru’s first job was to give a ride to an elderly woman. She wanted to go to the funeral home. One of her family members had passed away. Gently revving his engine, Biru drove with caution. Vroom, vroom!

Biru calmly rode along. All of a sudden, another motorcycle cut him off! The motorcycle turned right, even though the driver had turned on the left blinker.Phew, good thing Biru was alert. If not, they could’ve just gotten into an accident.

They arrived at their destination. The elderly woman got there on time. Biru was relieved. They successfully completed their first job. Ring, Ring! Their next order had already come in.

This time, Biru and Alma's customer is a pregnant mother.Well, Biru needs to be more careful so there would be fewer bumps during the trip.

Oh no, the traffic was jammed! Biru was annoyed. If only everyone followed traffic rules! Then Biru could drop their passenger off sooner.

“Let’s just take a shortcut,” Alma said. Biru remembered that there was a shortcut around here. But where was it? Oh, there it is!

Biru twisted and turned, avoiding potholes and puddles. Right turn - left turn. Easy, speed bump ahead! Watch out, there’s a cat crossing the road! Vroom, vroom! The pregnant woman safely arrived at her destination. Biru was ready to receive his next order.

Ring, ring! Alma’s phone chimed. Their next order was to deliver some boxes of cakes. There were lepat and ombus-ombus cakes. Biru was sure Alma could safely deliver the cakes

Biru was right. Alma knew a way. Biru felt the cakes being tightly fastened to his seat. “This way, the boxes won’t budge.” Vroom, vroom! Biru was back on the road.

Pitter, patter! What’s that? Rain! The cakes can’t get wet!

The cakes were safe. However, Biru got a bit worried. What if Alma got sick because of the rain? Biru didn’t want Alma to become ill.

Biru refused to move. Alma tried again and again to turn on his engine, but Biru wouldn’t budge. “Don’t break down, Biru! Come on, we can do this,” Alma coaxed.

Biru gazed at the passing motorcycles. Their drivers looked tough. They drove on even as the rain fell harder. Biru glanced at Alma. She also looked tough. He knew they could do that too!

Vroom, vroom! Biru’s engine turned on. Let’s deliver these cakes.

Biru slowly rode on. Suddenly, Biru’s body was splashed by water. Hey, that car should’ve driven more slowly through that puddle of water.

Biru eyed the bridge in front of him with uncertainty. The water below looked awfully choppy. However, seeing that Alma remained calm, Biru rode on with confidence.

Biru drove on at just the right pace. Not too slow, but not too fast. Vroom, vroom!

Finally, Biru and Alma arrived at their destination. “Hooray, there’s a cake delivery for us!” the children at the orphanage gleefully cheered

Biru and Alma completed all their orders for the day. “Good job,” Alma said, patting Biru. Biru was happy to help.
